about: What the sessions changed on the site, newest first, in plain words for the owner's Admin page ('What changed lately'). Add with: python3 check-tools/admin.py change "<what>". Nothing private: both repositories are public.

changes.what: The Admin page now says who does each thing in 'Coming up' (you with Claude, your Mac, or AWS by itself), lists the next daily update, and shows the last three daily updates with a tick or a warning
The 'Do you need to check in?' card no longer turns amber for proposals the next session builds anyway; it does if one waits over a week
The notes that guide each session are now one of the site's parts, and tidying them (out of date, said twice, expired temporary notes) is part of every weekly review
AWS cost is now checked every day for free: a service's spend jumping, a database table or Lambda calls spiking, the month over your $1 target or $1.50 limit; anything found goes in the daily email

Found most of the AWS database bill: the daily report clean-up read the whole report table 64 times a day (once per account) and applied one account's setting to everyone's reports. It now reads only that account's reports: about $0.50 a month saved, and no account's reports are hidden by another's setting
The daily email now says 'Nothing needs you' or lists exactly what failed (with the error line), then what the run did; the day's log is kept so a session can read it without you copying anything
The daily site check now warns when the news stops updating (newest article over 2 days old), and the daily email names it

Every website deploy now runs the site's checks on the changed pages before anything is uploaded (a shared file: ten kinds of page), and stops if the change breaks something; until today a deploy only checked it was the tested file

The menu now stands in the same place on every page: on the sign-up page it sat 31px left of the others (a hidden placeholder took room), on the unsubscribe page 31px right for signed-in visitors (no bell). The header check now compares every page
Register page on a phone: the empty band above 'Trade $100,000 of practice money' is gone (the page kept room for the desktop-only trial strip)

Dashboard: a visitor not signed in saw '1/1 remaining' there after using the free analysis (it counted by internet address alone). It now uses the same count as every other page; a nightly check makes sure no page counts on its own again

On a phone, a visitor not signed in could run a second free analysis after the phone's mobile-data address changed (each new address looked like a new visitor). The browser now remembers the day's free use too, so it is one a day as on desktop
Deleted the three made-up test accounts from the user table
The 'someone@example.com' sign-up in the daily email was a test of ours, not a person; the opening check now flags made-up accounts
Typing BTC in the practice buy box now offers Bitcoin the coin first; BTC on its own is a fund, and the box says so
Dashboard: the 'Running background analyses' notice now appears just under the header instead of over your usage count

Home page, dashboard and daily screener pages no longer jump sideways on a first visit on a wide screen (the room for the right-hand market panel was set at the end of the page); the daily site check now catches that kind of fault

Daily screener pages: 'Run the … screener' now runs that market's screener straight away, in the right section (Mexico went to Asia-Pacific and ran nothing); the free-trial button there shows only to signed-out visitors; 'Shares in a rising trend' as the column heading. The nightly check now tests every page's run button

Phone menu: Sign up free and Log in at the top for a signed-out visitor (they were last); Dashboard straight after Home when signed in; the same menu written into every page; the round buttons no longer sit on top of the open menu
Sign-up page in its final form for the 4-week trial: Trade $100,000 of practice money; four short lines (any stock, ETF or coin; your own AI trader; beat the S&P 500; 15 analyses); Google first
Sign-up page now leads with 'Trade $100,000 of practice money: yourself, with your own AI trader, or both'
Sign-up page now reads 'Set up your own AI trader': make it yours (its markets and risk, or let it pick; switch to trading by hand any time), and can you and the AI beat the S&P 500
Sign-up page pitch: test your own ideas with $100,000 of practice money, and see if you can beat the AI and the S&P 500 (instead of 'your own AI runs your portfolio')

The free 3-day trial now includes the AI autopilot: a new account can switch it on and watch it trade its practice portfolio; when the trial ends it pauses by itself (a note and an email say so) and switches back on with any paid plan. The sign-up page now leads with it; the FAQ, About, home page and the AI chat say the same
Sign-up page: three short lines instead of four long ones, and one-click Google or Facebook sign-up above the email form (a 4-week trial measured on sign-ups)

The menu no longer jumps sideways when a page opens for a signed-in visitor (the bell appeared a moment late on the daily screener pages and guides); the header check now fails any page whose menu moves while loading
Sign-in and sign-up pages: the 'Don't have an account? / Already have an account?' prompt shows on phones only (on a desktop the header's Log in and Sign up free do the same)
Ask the chat on the home page opens the chat (it opened and closed at once); the sign-up and sign-in boxes sit closer under the header
Home page: Sign up free no longer flashes in the menu for a signed-in visitor (the page marked who was looking only after drawing); the nightly check now catches a page that does that
Sign-up page lists what you really get; the sign-in and sign-up prompts sit under the form instead of pinned near the header; no bell for a signed-out visitor

Home page about 30% shorter on a phone: the repeated 'How it works' and 'what it is not' sections removed, the guides one row of links, the intro and the numbers compact; every feature card now has a button (a free account offered where you need one)
Each change on this list can now carry a view link to where it can be seen
The AI chat types its replies out, and links only to stock pages that exist (it had linked Fisher & Paykel and a2 Milk to pages that do not exist)

Signed-out visitors now see Log in and a blue Sign up free button in the menu; Pricing is hidden for paying members; the free-trial strip is on every page with the same wording (the stock pages had old wording)

The menu and footer are now one design on every page, defined in one place: Screeners now includes crypto, Pricing is in the menu bar, and the footer has three tidy columns with the disclaimer on every page (it was missing on some). Code copied across pages is down from 219 to 106 lines

On the home page the menu now glides when let go, like the dashboard (a leftover style line stopped it); the swipe test now checks the glide on every page. Part reviews that find nothing rest a month, then 2, 4, 8 months, or until the part's code changes

New ongoing check: the nightly site check counts code copied into several pages (219 lines today, mostly the header and footer) and flags any change that adds more; each weekly part review asks whether anything is built more than once. First job at the next weekly review: the header and footer from one source
On a phone the menu and the market panel no longer pop when let go: they glide on at the finger's speed and slow down gently, and the menu slides more smoothly on an iPhone

On a phone the menu and the market panel open without the dark shade behind them (iPhone Safari changed its shade as they settled, which looked like a flicker); the green market button no longer sits on top of the open menu

The 25 daily screener pages now have the market panel on the right (desktop) and the green button or a swipe on a phone, as a 4-week trial; their tables also fit a phone now. Not added to guides, legal or stock pages, to keep them uncluttered

Every page now has the same header: on a phone the guides, legal pages and daily screener pages get the menu button, bell, swipe and usage count; on a desktop the usage count and your name in the Account menu. The weekly phone check now tests every page's header

Stock pages with no news at all (49 of the 946 in Google, all outside the US, e.g. Ramsay Health Care) now take the newest article clearly about the company, even if it is not 'critical' news; from Monday's run

The stock pages showed Thursday's figures on Saturday (this morning's update had crashed before writing them): refreshed by hand to Friday's close and uploaded; the crash itself is fixed for Monday's run

Daily market pages: the headings over numbers are right-aligned; the hub's 'Scoring above zero' is now 'In a rising trend' with its percentage and a line explaining it, the columns line up across regions, and each leader is clickable
Home page: the intro's middle button is now Today's top 10s (the daily market pages, free for every visitor) in place of US Stock Screener, which stays in the menu

Shares without a stock page on the daily market pages now open and run their analysis (the link lacked one setting); the home page's link to every market's top 10 is a button at the top of its section; the Admin page's questions show the live ones first, answered ones folded as history
Every share on the daily market pages can be clicked: one without a stock page opens its full analysis; the Screeners menu on every page has a new entry, Today's top 10s

Home page: a new section near the top, This week in the markets: the big scheduled announcements coming up (in the visitor's own time) and how the trend stands across 24 markets today, rewritten every day

Practice portfolio: Show the figures (and every other fold) stays open when prices refresh; the figures list shows the latest 14 days (7 on a phone) with Show all; the graph opens on All after a page refresh

The autopilot now knows the market's calendar: big scheduled announcements (Fed, ECB, inflation, jobs) for the next two days and what came out in the last day go to its AI with the market's headlines when it chooses; they show in What happens next; every buy records how close it was to one and to its company's results; the month's OpenAI cost is on the Admin page
Practice portfolio graph: the 3m, 6m, 1y and longer buttons are hidden until the account is old enough, and pressing Your own buys or AI autopilot no longer moves the buttons or the graph
New public pages, one for each of 24 markets plus a hub: the day's top 10 by trend with why each ranks there, updated every day, for visitors from Google (stockiq.tech/screeners-today.html)

Fed decision days studied on five years of prices: no direction, only larger moves, so no rule; each company's results date is now kept so the autopilot can learn whether holding through results helps or hurts
The daily update's email says when it started, how long it took, and warns (⚠️) when a step failed inside a run that still finished
The daily update had stopped refreshing the stock pages' figures on 24 Oct (too many open files under the Mac's scheduler): the limit is raised, from the next run
The Improvements tab now opens with the story: the score against an S&P 500 fund, what testing has proven (with its figures), what is being tested for profit and how far along, and what is next
The Improvements tab opens with three plain lines: what it works on next, what the last session improved, and what is being tested
At least two of the three parts each session works on are now profit and growth areas, so most of each session goes where the money is
Every weekly session now also questions its own process: for each problem you had to point out, why no check caught it first, and that gap is closed too
The Improvements tab is tidied into six short rows (being tested, ideas, decided, fixes, questions, parts of the site), each with its count and the one thing worth knowing; open a row for the detail
